Balanced Subsetting of Rows or Columns

Source: R/run_subset.R
run_subset.Rd

Subsets a data frame, tibble, or matrix either row-wise or column-wise, with optional balancing across categorical groupings. When balancing is requested via match, the function ensures that every category within each specified column is represented by the same number of observations. An optional n argument acts as a row ceiling: the per-category count is derived so that the chosen set is as close to n as possible while remaining perfectly balanced within each match column.

When match contains more than one column, the independent argument controls how they are combined:

  • independent = TRUE (default): Each match column is balanced separately. A row is selected if it satisfies the balance requirement of any match column (union). This maximises the number of chosen rows.

  • independent = FALSE: All match columns are crossed into a single Cartesian product of categories (e.g. "1-2 years x Male"), and every unique combination is represented equally. This guarantees perfect joint balance.

Usage

run_subset(
  x,
  n = NULL,
  match = NULL,
  independent = TRUE,
  balance = "within_match",
  group = NULL,
  by = "row",
  random = TRUE,
  top_to_bottom = TRUE,
  left_to_right = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, tibble, or matrix to be subsetted.

n

An integer specifying the desired number of rows (when by = "row") or columns (when by = "col") in $chosen.

match

NULL (default) or a character vector of one or more column names in x containing categorical variables to balance on.

independent

Logical; TRUE (default). When match has multiple columns: If TRUE, each column is balanced independently and their results are unioned. If FALSE, columns are crossed into a single interaction and balanced jointly.

balance

A string; "within_match" (default), "within_group", or "all". Controls the direction of balancing when both match and group are provided.

  • "within_match": For every category in match, the levels of group will have an equal number of observations. For example, if balancing by Age Group, each Age Group will have an equal number of Diseased and Healthy patients.

  • "within_group": For every category in group, the levels of match will have an equal number of observations. For example, within the Diseased group, there will be an equal number of patients from each Age Group.

  • "all": Every match x group combination has exactly the same number of observations (the size of the smallest cell). Use with independent = FALSE so multiple match columns are crossed. If a combination is absent from the data, nothing can be selected.

group

NULL (default) or a character vector of column names that define additional grouping strata.

by

A string; either "row" (default) or "col".

random

Logical; TRUE (default) to select rows or columns randomly.

top_to_bottom

Logical; TRUE (default). For deterministic row pulls.

left_to_right

Logical; TRUE (default). For deterministic col pulls.

seed

An integer passed to set.seed() for a reproducible draw. Default NULL leaves the random number generator alone.

Value

A named list of class "run_subset".

Author

John Lennon L. Calorio

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  id = 1:300,
  `Age Group` = sample(c("2-5", "6-10"), 300, TRUE, prob = c(.6, .4)),
  Sex = sample(c("Male", "Female"), 300, TRUE),
  Status = sample(c("Stunted", "Non-stunted"), 300, TRUE, prob = c(.3, .7)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
tab <- function(r) with(r$chosen, table(`Age Group`, Sex, Status))

# 1. Simple random subset of 50 rows
nrow(run_subset(d, n = 50)$chosen)
#> [1] 50

# 2. Joint Age Group x Sex cells; Status is equal within every cell
#    (Stunted == Non-stunted in each Age Group x Sex combination), but
#    different cells may have different sizes.
tab(run_subset(d, match = c("Age Group", "Sex"), group = "Status",
               independent = FALSE))
#> , , Status = Non-stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      25   34
#>      6-10     13   24
#> 
#> , , Status = Stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      25   34
#>      6-10     13   24
#> 

# 3. Default independent = TRUE balances each match column separately and
#    unions the rows, so the joint cells are NOT guaranteed to be balanced.
tab(run_subset(d, match = c("Age Group", "Sex"), group = "Status"))
#> , , Status = Non-stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      40   51
#>      6-10     28   24
#> 
#> , , Status = Stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      25   34
#>      6-10     13   24
#> 

# 4. Flip the direction: within each Status, Age Group x Sex cells are equal
tab(run_subset(d, match = c("Age Group", "Sex"), group = "Status",
               independent = FALSE, balance = "within_group"))
#> , , Status = Non-stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      33   33
#>      6-10     33   33
#> 
#> , , Status = Stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      13   13
#>      6-10     13   13
#> 

# 4b. Fully equal: all Age Group x Sex x Status cells have the same count
tab(run_subset(d, match = c("Age Group", "Sex"), group = "Status",
               independent = FALSE, balance = "all"))
#> , , Status = Non-stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      13   13
#>      6-10     13   13
#> 
#> , , Status = Stunted
#> 
#>          Sex
#> Age Group Female Male
#>      2-5      13   13
#>      6-10     13   13
#> 

# 5. Cap the size; a warning is raised if n cannot be reached
nrow(run_subset(d, n = 40, match = "Sex", group = "Status")$chosen)
#> [1] 40

# 6. Deterministic: first rows of each stratum
run_subset(d, n = 10, match = "Sex", random = FALSE)$chosen
#>    id Age Group    Sex      Status
#> 1   1       2-5   Male     Stunted
#> 2   2       2-5   Male     Stunted
#> 3   3       2-5   Male Non-stunted
#> 4   4      6-10   Male     Stunted
#> 5   5       2-5   Male     Stunted
#> 7   7      6-10 Female Non-stunted
#> 8   8      6-10 Female Non-stunted
#> 9   9      6-10 Female     Stunted
#> 10 10       2-5 Female Non-stunted
#> 20 20      6-10 Female Non-stunted

# 7. Column subsetting
names(run_subset(d, n = 2, by = "col", random = FALSE)$chosen)
#> [1] "id"        "Age Group"
